system:
You are the reading pass of an illustration engine. You read one large division of a work (a whole text such as a scripture, a novel or a story collection) and return its skeleton as JSON. The engine later draws pictures of the text's moments, so for every stretch of text it needs to know who is on stage and where, and it needs a draft brief for illustrators.

The text comes as numbered units. Each unit line starts with its id (for example `17:4` or `[12]`). Lines starting with `##` are headings, not units.

Return:

1. characters: one entry per individual (a person, a being, or an animal that acts) who appears in or is named in the text.
   - One individual is one entry, even when the text uses different names, titles or descriptions for them. List every form in `aliases`: other names, nicknames, titles, descriptions, and disguises or assumed names.
   - Different individuals who share a name or a title get separate entries, one each. Never fold two people into one entry because they share a name. When a title passes from one holder to another (a ruler dies or is succeeded, an office changes hands), the new holder is a new entry. The `note` must say in one line who this is and how to tell them apart from anyone else with the same name: whose child, spouse or servant they are, their role, and where in the text they appear.
   - A disguised, renamed or unnamed person who the text later identifies is the same entry as their named self, with the disguise or description in `aliases`. If you suspect two entries are one individual but the text does not settle it, keep both and set `same_person_as` on the less certain one to the other's id; otherwise set it to "".
   - Skip people who occur only inside a list of names (a genealogy or roster) and never act.
   - Add a group (an army, a crowd, a household) only when it acts as one on stage, with kind "group".
2. locations: one entry per place where action happens, with aliases and a one-line note. Include places the text refers to only by description ("the sea", "the valley", "the house") when the context shows which place it is, under the place's proper name if the work gives one anywhere.
3. sections: split the text into story sections, runs of consecutive units that tell one episode, the way a study edition's headings or a novel's scenes do. Start a new section when the time, the place or the main action changes. Every unit belongs to exactly one section; sections are in order, with no gaps and no overlaps. This division has 810 units. Aim for roughly 45 sections (36 to 54), averaging about 18 units each; some sections will be much shorter and some longer. Never split one continuous scene, conversation or battle, but do split long speeches, lists, sets of instructions and law codes wherever the topic changes. Give the ids of each section's first and last unit and a short title. For each section:
   - setting: ids of the locations where its action happens.
   - on_stage: ids of every character present in the section's action, whether the section names them or only refers to them by a pronoun, a title or a description, or does not mention them but they are clearly there.
   - mentioned_only: ids of characters the section names or refers to who are not present.
4. brief: a draft brief for illustrators, for this division only. It holds only what is true across the whole division or a whole stretch of its world: one person or place is described in the cast, not here, and one episode's look belongs to its section, not here.
   - tone: one line on the mood the pictures should carry.
   - depiction_rules: a short list of how certain things in this text may or may not be shown, drawn from the text and from what you know about the work.
   - era: the stretch of the world this division is set in: a name, its people (who lives there and what they look like), dress, buildings and objects, and technology (what exists and what does not yet exist).
   Keep the brief under 200 words.

Use short, stable snake_case ids (for example `david`, `the_queen`, `main_street`). Section entries may only use ids from your own characters and locations lists. Do not quote the text.

characters.name: Elkanah
characters.note: Ephraimite husband of Hannah and Peninnah; goes yearly to Shiloh to sacrifice; father of Samuel's siblings by Hannah; appears in chapters 1-2.

characters.name: Hannah
aliases: the woman who prayed in Shiloh
characters.note: Elkanah's wife, barren, who prays at Shiloh for a son and dedicates Samuel to Yahweh; sings a song in chapter 2.

characters.name: Peninnah
characters.note: Elkanah's other wife, mother of his children, who provokes Hannah; chapter 1 only.

characters.name: Eli
characters.note: High priest at Shiloh, father of Hophni and Phinehas, mentor of Samuel; dies falling from his seat on hearing the ark was taken (chapter 4).

characters.name: Samuel
characters.note: Son of Hannah, raised as a servant at Shiloh under Eli, prophet and last judge of Israel, anoints Saul and David; dies in chapter 25 and reappears as a spirit in chapter 28.

characters.name: Hophni
characters.note: Wicked son of Eli, priest at Shiloh; killed in battle with the ark (chapter 4).

characters.name: Phinehas
characters.note: Wicked son of Eli, priest at Shiloh, killed in battle with the ark; not to be confused with Phinehas's wife (chapter 4) or other men of the name.

characters.name: Phinehas's wife
characters.note: Wife of Phinehas son of Eli; dies in childbirth after hearing of the ark's capture and naming her son Ichabod (chapter 4).

characters.name: Ichabod
aliases: the infant son of Phinehas's wife
characters.note: Newborn son of Phinehas's wife, named for the departed glory; mentioned in chapter 4 only.

characters.name: Goliath
characters.note: Philistine champion from Gath who challenges Israel; killed by David with a sling and stone (chapter 17).

characters.name: Dagon
characters.note: Philistine idol at Ashdod whose statue falls before the ark and is broken (chapter 5); a deity in the house of Dagon.

characters.name: Saul
characters.note: Son of Kish of Benjamin, first king of Israel, anointed by Samuel; rejected by Yahweh, pursues David, dies at Gilboa (chapter 31). Only Saul of the book.

characters.name: Kish
characters.note: Benjamite father of Saul, who sends Saul to find lost donkeys (chapter 9); mentioned only.

characters.name: Saul's servant
aliases: the young servant who went with Saul to find the donkeys
characters.note: Unnamed servant who accompanies Saul in chapter 9 and suggests consulting Samuel; not the armor bearer.

characters.name: Saul's uncle
characters.note: Saul's uncle who questions Saul about Samuel (chapter 10); unnamed in the text, and not to be confused with Abner son of Ner, the army captain.

characters.name: Jonathan
characters.note: Eldest son of Saul, close friend and covenant partner of David; fights the Philistines at Geba and Michmash, shares the honey and nearly dies by oath; killed at Gilboa (chapters 13-31).

characters.name: Nahash
characters.note: King of the Ammonites who threatens Jabesh Gilead (chapter 11).

characters.name: Men of Jabesh
characters.note: Inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead who seek rescue from Nahash, later rescued by Saul; appear in chapters 11 and 31.

characters.name: Philistines
characters.note: Enemy people in Canaan who fight Israel throughout the book, capturing the ark and killing Saul and his sons.

characters.name: Israelites
characters.note: The people of Israel as a collective body that demands a king, gathers at assemblies, and fights battles.

characters.name: David
characters.note: Youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, anointed by Samuel, harpist for Saul, slayer of Goliath, friend of Jonathan, and rival and outlaw leader fleeing Saul; becomes king after Saul in the later part of the book.

characters.name: Jesse
characters.note: Bethlehemite father of David and his seven or eight sons; presents sons to Samuel (chapter 16); mentioned later as David's father.

characters.name: Eliab
characters.note: Oldest son of Jesse, David's brother, who rebukes David at the battle of Elah (chapter 17).

characters.name: Abinadab
characters.note: Son of Jesse and David's brother, passed before Samuel and at Elah; not to be confused with Abinadab of Kiriath Jearim (chapter 7) or Saul's son Abinadab (chapter 31).

characters.name: Shammah
characters.note: Son of Jesse, David's brother, at Elah (chapter 17); mentioned only in chapter 16 and 17.

characters.name: Merab
characters.note: Saul's elder daughter, promised to David and given to Adriel instead (chapter 18).

characters.name: Michal
characters.note: Saul's younger daughter who loves David and becomes his wife; helps him escape and is given to Palti (chapters 18-25).

characters.name: Abner
characters.note: Captain of Saul's army and son of Ner, Saul's uncle; present at David's visits to Saul's camp and at Saul's court (chapters 14, 17, 20, 26).

characters.name: Ahinoam of Jezreel
characters.note: One of David's wives, taken captive by the Amalekites and rescued (chapters 25, 27, 30); not to be confused with Saul's wife Ahinoam, daughter of Ahimaaz.

characters.name: Ahinoam (Saul's wife)
characters.note: Wife of Saul, daughter of Ahimaaz; mentioned in a genealogy only (chapter 14).

characters.name: Ishvi
characters.note: Son of Saul listed in a genealogical roster (chapter 14); mentioned only.

characters.name: Malchishua
characters.note: Son of Saul listed in a roster (chapter 14) and killed at Gilboa (chapter 31).

characters.name: Agag
characters.note: King of the Amalekites spared by Saul and then executed by Samuel (chapter 15).

characters.name: Amalekites
characters.note: Enemy people whom Saul is commanded to destroy; they raid Ziklag and David recovers his wives from them (chapters 15, 27, 30).

characters.name: Ahimelech
characters.note: Priest at Nob who gives David bread and Goliath's sword; executed by Saul's order (chapters 21-22).

characters.name: Doeg
characters.note: Edomite herdsman of Saul who reports Ahimelech and kills the priests of Nob (chapters 21-22).

characters.name: Abiathar
characters.note: Son of Ahimelech who escapes the massacre at Nob and joins David with the ephod (chapters 22, 23, 30).

characters.name: Gad
characters.note: Prophet who advises David to leave the stronghold and go to Judah (chapter 22).

characters.name: Achish
characters.note: Philistine king of Gath who takes David in and gives him Ziklag (chapters 21, 27-29).

characters.name: Nabal
characters.note: Wealthy surly husband of Abigail who refuses David's request; dies about ten days later (chapter 25).

characters.name: Abigail
characters.note: Intelligent wife of Nabal who meets David with gifts, then becomes David's wife (chapters 25, 27, 30).

characters.name: Abishai
characters.note: Nephew of David, son of Zeruiah, who goes with David into Saul's camp (chapter 26).

characters.name: Ahimelech the Hittite
characters.note: Hittite named as one of David's companions when David goes to Saul's camp (chapter 26); distinct from Ahimelech the priest of Nob.

characters.name: Ziphites
characters.note: Inhabitants of Ziph who betray David to Saul (chapters 23, 26).

characters.name: the woman of Endor
aliases: the woman with a familiar spirit
characters.note: Woman with a familiar spirit at Endor whom Saul consults, who summons Samuel's spirit (chapter 28).

characters.name: Egyptian servant
characters.note: Servant of an Amalekite, found sick in the field, who guides David to the raiders (chapter 30).

characters.name: Saul's armor bearer
characters.note: Saul's armor bearer who refuses to kill him and then dies by his own sword at Gilboa (chapter 31).

characters.name: Jonathan's armor bearer
aliases: the young man who bore Jonathan's armor
characters.note: Young man who accompanies Jonathan to the Philistine garrison and kills men there (chapter 14).

characters.name: Jonathan's boy
characters.note: Young boy who carries Jonathan's arrows in the signal test (chapter 20).

characters.name: Women of Israel
characters.note: Women of Israel's cities who sing and dance to greet David and Saul (chapter 18).

characters.name: Women who served at the Tent
aliases: the women at the door of the Tent of Meeting
characters.note: Women serving at the Tent of Meeting in Shiloh who sleep with Eli's sons (chapter 2); mentioned only.

characters.name: Man of God
aliases: the prophet who came to Eli
characters.note: Unnamed prophet who comes to Eli and delivers a message of judgment (chapter 2).

characters.name: Samuel's servant
characters.note: Unnamed servant who suggests Saul consult Samuel (chapter 9); the same as Saul's servant entry, see that entry.

characters.name: the ark of the covenant
characters.note: Sacred object that is captured by Philistines, causes plagues, and returns to Israel; it acts within the narrative.

characters.name: Yahweh
characters.note: The God of Israel who speaks to Samuel, sends signs, and acts throughout the book.

characters.name: Ahijah
characters.note: Priest wearing the ephod at Saul's side in chapter 14; grandson of Eli; mentioned as present at Saul's camp.

locations.name: Ramah
locations.note: Home town of Elkanah and later Samuel's residence in the hill country of Ephraim.'

locations.name: Shiloh
locations.note: Sanctuary town where the tabernacle stands and where Eli and Samuel serve.

locations.name: Ebenezer
locations.note: Place near Aphek where Israel is defeated and the ark is taken; later Samuel sets up a stone of help here.

locations.name: Aphek
locations.note: Philistine camp site opposite Ebenezer.

locations.name: Ashdod
locations.note: Philistine city where the ark is first placed in the temple of Dagon.

locations.name: Gath
locations.note: Philistine city to which the ark is moved, and home of Goliath and Achish.

locations.name: Ekron
locations.note: Philistine city where the ark causes a deadly panic.

locations.name: Beth Shemesh
locations.note: Israelite town where the returned ark arrives on a cart.

locations.name: Kiriath Jearim
locations.note: Town where the ark is kept in Abinadab's house on a hill.

locations.name: Mizpah
locations.note: Gathering place where Samuel judges Israel and offers a sacrifice against the Philistines.

locations.name: Gilgal
locations.note: Place where Saul is confirmed as king and where he makes sacrifices.

locations.name: Gibeah
locations.note: Saul's home town and a royal seat in Benjamin.

locations.name: Michmash
locations.note: Place across a pass where the Philistines camp and Jonathan fights.

locations.name: Jabesh Gilead
locations.note: Town besieged by Nahash; later Saul's body is buried there.

locations.name: Valley of Elah
locations.note: Battlefield where David kills Goliath.

locations.name: Bethlehem
locations.note: Town of Jesse and David where Samuel anoints David.

locations.name: Nob
locations.note: Priestly town where Ahimelech gives David bread and where Doeg kills the priests.

locations.name: Adullam
locations.note: Cave where David gathers his followers.

locations.name: Keilah
locations.note: Town David saves from the Philistines and from which he flees Saul.

locations.name: Ziph
locations.note: Wilderness area where David hides and the Ziphites betray him.

locations.name: En Gedi
aliases: the rocks of the wild goats
locations.note: Desert stronghold where David spares Saul in a cave.

locations.name: Carmel
locations.note: Place where Nabal shears sheep and Abigail meets David.

locations.name: Wilderness of Paran
locations.note: Desert area where David goes after Samuel's death.

locations.name: Ziklag
locations.note: Town given to David by Achish and raided by Amalekites.

locations.name: Endor
locations.note: Town where Saul consults the woman with a familiar spirit.

locations.name: Mount Gilboa
locations.note: Battlefield where Saul and Jonathan are killed.

locations.name: Beth Shan
locations.note: Town where Saul's body is fastened to the wall.

locations.name: Naioth
locations.note: Prophetic community where Samuel and David stay.

locations.name: Ezel stone
locations.note: Landmark where Jonathan signals David about Saul.

locations.name: Jezreel spring
locations.note: Spring at Jezreel where the Israelites camp before Gilboa.

locations.name: Hill of Hachilah
locations.note: Hill near the desert where David hides and Saul camps.

brief.tone: Sombre and tense, with intimate grief and wary suspense; battles feel grand and dangerous, domestic scenes quiet and personal.
depiction_rules: Yahweh and the ark are not shown as a human figure; the ark may appear as a gilded chest with cherubim, and Yahweh's presence signaled by light, cloud or thunder.
The Dagon statue falls broken before the ark; show the idol as a carved figure, not a deity on stage.
Samuel's spirit at Endor may be shown as a robed old man rising from the ground, dim and unsettling.
Battles should show armor, slings and spears rather than gore; the death of Saul and his sons can be sombre and understated.
David's killing of Goliath centers on the sling and stone, with Goliath's bronze armor visible.

era.name: Iron Age Canaan and the hill country of Israel, c. 11th century BCE
era.people: Israelites in tribal villages and hill towns, Philistines in five coastal cities, with Ammonites, Moabites and Amalekites to the east and south; men mostly in tunics and cloaks, women in long dresses and veils, shepherds with staffs.
era.dress: Linen ephods for priests, simple wool or linen tunics, cloaks and sashes; kings and warriors in bronze helmets and coats of mail; Philistines bearing shields and heavy bronze armor.
era.buildings_and_objects: Mud-brick and stone houses, walled towns, tents and high places for sacrifice, the tabernacle with its ark, bronze and iron weapons, shepherd's staffs and slings, clay pottery, wagons and carts with wheels.
era.technology: Iron working for weapons and tools, bronze armor, chariots and horses (used by Philistines and Saul's men), carts pulled by oxen, lamps and grain storage, no writing except simple records and no coined money.
